## Blocked-sender hooks: VTC, Scene and Graph each pass a different account (and Scene/Graph lose the recipient's account)
Crates: jmap-scene-server, jmap-graph-server (jmap-vtc-server and jmap-chat-vtc-server for comparison)
Evidence: The probe builds one Deploy struct that implements ChatBackend, VtcBackend, SceneBackend and GraphBackend, and sends all three extension block hooks through jmap_chat_vtc_server::is_blocked_by_contact(chat, caller, account_id, user_id). VTC: crate-jmap-vtc-server/src/backend.rs:487 `is_user_blocked(caller, account_id, user_id: &str)`. Its docs say account_id is the recipient's own account, and ephemeral.rs:215/229/285 pass `recipient_account_id`, so it forwards directly. Scene: crate-jmap-scene-server/src/backend.rs:608 `is_user_blocked(caller, user_id: &str)` takes no account at all. scene-server/src/ephemeral.rs:269-270 has `recipient_account_id` in scope (it uses it for has_capability on the line before) and drops it on the is_user_blocked call. Graph: crate-jmap-graph-server/src/backend.rs:357 `is_sender_blocked(caller, account_id, sender_id: &Id)`. Here graph-server/src/stream.rs:144-147 and :191 pass the event's accountId, which is the node's *hosting* account. graph `should_deliver` (stream.rs:134) has no recipient_account_id parameter, unlike vtc should_deliver and scene should_deliver / chat-scene should_deliver_scene. Spec: draft-atwood-jmap-scene-wss-00 L790-797 says the server consults "the recipient's ChatContact records" when Chat "is available for the receiving account". draft-atwood-jmap-graph-edit-00 L370 says not to deliver to "a user who has blocked the sender". ChatContacts are per-account records. Workaround in the probe: add `own_account: Id` to CallerCtx and ignore the hook's account argument (probe src/lib.rs `Ctx`, SceneBackend::is_user_blocked, GraphBackend::is_sender_blocked).
Why breaking later: Adding an account parameter to SceneBackend::is_user_blocked or changing what GraphBackend::is_sender_blocked's account_id means changes a public trait method signature or its contract. Adding recipient_account_id to jmap_graph_server::should_deliver changes a pub fn signature. Each one breaks every downstream impl and caller. Until it is fixed, the Graph hook's parameter named account_id invites an implementer to look up ChatContacts in the hosting account. For a node in a shared account, that looks in the wrong account and silently delivers cursors from blocked users (fails open). Scene implementers have to smuggle the account through CallerCtx. The sibling shapes also differ from each other, which goes against the cookie-cutter rule for extension servers in AGENTS.md Canonical Templates.
Fix: Make the three hooks one shape before 0.4: `(caller, recipient_account_id: &Id, user)`, matching VTC. In SceneBackend::is_user_blocked, add `account_id: &Id` and pass `recipient_account_id` from ephemeral.rs:270. In jmap_graph_server::should_deliver, add `recipient_account_id: &Id` (as the VTC and Scene should_deliver already have) and pass it to is_sender_blocked; document account_id as the recipient's own account. Keep sender_id as a Principal Id, because draft-atwood-jmap-graph-edit-00 L362 defines senderId that way.
Size: S
